"chunk 1 | chars: 1444-3554 | source: installation.mdx\n### Configure Database\n\nBetter Auth requires a database to store user data.\nYou can easily configure Better Auth to use SQLite, PostgreSQL, or MySQL, and more!\n\n<Tabs items={[\"sqlite\", \"postgres\", \"mysql\"]}>\n    <Tab value=\"sqlite\">\n    ```ts title=\"auth.ts\"\n    import { betterAuth } from \"better-auth\";\n    import Database from \"better-sqlite3\";\n\n    export const auth = betterAuth({\n        database: new Database(\"./sqlite.db\"),\n    })\n    ```\n    </Tab>\n    <Tab value=\"postgres\">\n    ```ts title=\"auth.ts\"\n    import { betterAuth } from \"better-auth\";\n    import { Pool } from \"pg\";\n\n    export const auth = betterAuth({\n        database: new Pool({\n            // connection options\n        }),\n    })\n    ```\n    </Tab>\n    <Tab value=\"mysql\">\n    ```ts title=\"auth.ts\"\n    import { betterAuth } from \"better-auth\";\n    import { createPool } from \"mysql2/promise\";\n\n    export const auth = betterAuth({\n        database: createPool({\n            // connection options\n        }),\n    })\n    ```\n    </Tab>\n\n</Tabs>\n\nAlternatively, if you prefer to use an ORM, you can use one of the built-in adapters.\n\n<Tabs items={[\"drizzle\", \"prisma\", \"mongodb\"]}>\n\n    <Tab value=\"drizzle\">\n    ```ts title=\"auth.ts\"\n    import { betterAuth } from \"better-auth\";\n    import { drizzleAdapter } from \"better-auth/adapters/drizzle\";\n    import { db } from \"@/db\"; // your drizzle instance\n\n    export const auth = betterAuth({\n        database: drizzleAdapter(db, {\n            provider: \"pg\", // or \"mysql\", \"sqlite\"\n        }),\n    });\n    ```\n    </Tab>\n    <Tab value=\"prisma\">\n        ```ts title=\"auth.ts\"\n        import { betterAuth } from \"better-auth\";\n        import { prismaAdapter } from \"better-auth/adapters/prisma\";\n        // If your Prisma file is located elsewhere, you can change the path\n        import { PrismaClient } from \"@/generated/prisma\";\n\n        const prisma = new PrismaClient();\n        export const auth = betterAuth({\n            database: prismaAdapter(prisma, {\n                provider: \"sqlite\", // or \"mysql\", \"postgresql\", ...etc\n            }),\n        });\n    ```\n    </Tab>\n\n\n\n---\n\nchunk 2 | chars: 0-2052 | source: database.mdx\n---\ntitle: Database\ndescription: Learn how to use a database with Better Auth.\n---\n\n## Adapters\n\nBetter Auth requires a database connection to store data. The database will be used to store data such as users, sessions, and more. Plugins can also define their own database tables to store data.\n\nYou can pass a database connection to Better Auth by passing a supported database instance in the database options. You can learn more about supported database adapters in the [Other relational databases](/docs/adapters/other-relational-databases) documentation.\n\n## CLI\n\nBetter Auth comes with a CLI tool to manage database migrations and generate schema.\n\n### Running Migrations\n\nThe cli checks your database and prompts you to add missing tables or update existing ones with new columns. This is only supported for the built-in Kysely adapter. For other adapters, you can use the `generate` command to create the schema and handle the migration through your ORM.\n\n```bash\nnpx @better-auth/cli migrate\n```\n\n### Generating Schema\n\nBetter Auth also provides a `generate` command to generate the schema required by Better Auth. The `generate` command creates the schema required by Better Auth. If you're using a database adapter like Prisma or Drizzle, this command will generate the right schema for your ORM. If you're using the built-in Kysely adapter, it will generate an SQL file you can run directly on your database.\n\n```bash\nnpx @better-auth/cli generate\n```\n\nSee the [CLI](/docs/concepts/cli) documentation for more information on the CLI.\n\n<Callout>\n  If you prefer adding tables manually, you can do that as well. The core schema\n  required by Better Auth is described below and you can find additional schema\n  required by plugins in the plugin documentation.\n</Callout>\n\n## Secondary Storage\n\nSecondary storage in Better Auth allows you to use key-value stores for managing session data, rate limiting counters, etc. This can be useful when you want to offload the storage of this intensive records to a high performance storage or even RAM.\n\n\n\n---\n\nchunk 3 | chars: 0-1443 | source: drizzle.mdx\n---\ntitle: Drizzle ORM Adapter\ndescription: Integrate Better Auth with Drizzle ORM.\n---\n\nDrizzle ORM is a powerful and flexible ORM for Node.js and TypeScript. It provides a simple and intuitive API for working with databases, and supports a wide range of databases including MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQLite, and more.\nRead more here: [Drizzle ORM](https://orm.drizzle.team/).\n\n## Example Usage\n\nMake sure you have Drizzle installed and configured.\nThen, you can use the Drizzle adapter to connect to your database.\n\n```ts title=\"auth.ts\"\nimport { betterAuth } from \"better-auth\";\nimport { drizzleAdapter } from \"better-auth/adapters/drizzle\";\nimport { db } from \"./database.ts\";\n\nexport const auth = betterAuth({\n  database: drizzleAdapter(db, {\n    // [!code highlight]\n    provider: \"sqlite\", // or \"pg\" or \"mysql\" // [!code highlight]\n  }), // [!code highlight]\n  //... the rest of your config\n});\n```\n\n## Schema generation & migration\n\nThe [Better Auth CLI](/docs/concepts/cli) allows you to generate or migrate\nyour database schema based on your Better Auth configuration and plugins.\n\nTo generate the schema required by Better Auth, run the following command:\n\n```bash title=\"Schema Generation\"\nnpx @better-auth/cli@latest generate\n```\n\nTo generate and apply the migration, run the following commands:\n\n```bash title=\"Schema Migration\"\nnpx drizzle-kit generate # generate the migration file\nnpx drizzle-kit migrate # apply the migration\n```\n\n\n\n---\n\nchunk 4 | chars: 1443-2425 | source: drizzle.mdx\n## Additional Information\n\nThe Drizzle adapter expects the schema you define to match the table names. For example, if your Drizzle schema maps the `user` table to `users`, you need to manually pass the schema and map it to the user table.\n\n```ts\nimport { betterAuth } from \"better-auth\";\nimport { db } from \"./drizzle\";\nimport { drizzleAdapter } from \"better-auth/adapters/drizzle\";\nimport { schema } from \"./schema\";\n\nexport const auth = betterAuth({\n  database: drizzleAdapter(db, {\n    provider: \"sqlite\", // or \"pg\" or \"mysql\"\n    schema: {\n      ...schema,\n      user: schema.users,\n    },\n  }),\n});\n```\n\nIf all your tables are using plural form, you can just pass the `usePlural` option:\n```ts\nexport const auth = betterAuth({\n  database: drizzleAdapter(db, {\n    ...\n    usePlural: true,\n  }),\n});\n```\n\nIf you're looking for performance improvements or tips, take a look at our guide to <Link href=\"/docs/guides/optimizing-for-performance\">performance optimizations</Link>.\n\n\n---\n\nchunk 5 | chars: 0-1909 | source: cli.mdx\n---\ntitle: CLI\ndescription: Built-in CLI for managing your project.\n---\n\nBetter Auth comes with a built-in CLI to help you manage the database schemas, initialize your project, generate a secret key for your application, and gather diagnostic information about your setup.\n\n## Generate\n\nThe `generate` command creates the schema required by Better Auth. If you're using a database adapter like Prisma or Drizzle, this command will generate the right schema for your ORM. If you're using the built-in Kysely adapter, it will generate an SQL file you can run directly on your database.\n\n```bash title=\"Terminal\"\nnpx @better-auth/cli@latest generate\n```\n\n### Options\n\n- `--output` - Where to save the generated schema. For Prisma, it will be saved in prisma/schema.prisma. For Drizzle, it goes to schema.ts in your project root. For Kysely, it's an SQL file saved as schema.sql in your project root.\n- `--config` - The path to your Better Auth config file. By default, the CLI will search for an auth.ts file in **./**, **./utils**, **./lib**, or any of these directories under the `src` directory.\n- `--yes` - Skip the confirmation prompt and generate the schema directly.\n\n\n## Migrate\n\nThe migrate command applies the Better Auth schema directly to your database. This is available if you're using the built-in Kysely adapter. For other adapters, you'll need to apply the schema using your ORM's migration tool.\n\n```bash title=\"Terminal\"\nnpx @better-auth/cli@latest migrate\n```\n\n### Options\n\n- `--config` - The path to your Better Auth config file. By default, the CLI will search for an auth.ts file in **./**, **./utils**, **./lib**, or any of these directories under the `src` directory.\n- `--yes` - Skip the confirmation prompt and apply the schema directly.\n\n## Init\n\nThe `init` command allows you to initialize Better Auth in your project.\n\n```bash title=\"Terminal\"\nnpx @better-auth/cli@latest init\n```\n\n\n\n---\n\nchunk 6 | chars: 0-767 | source: other-relational-databases.mdx\n---\ntitle: Other Relational Databases\ndescription: Integrate Better Auth with other relational databases.\n---\n\nBetter Auth supports a wide range of database dialects out of the box thanks to <Link href=\"https://kysely.dev/\">Kysely</Link>.\n\nAny dialect supported by Kysely can be utilized with Better Auth, including capabilities for generating and migrating database schemas through the <Link href=\"/docs/concepts/cli\">CLI</Link>.\n\n## Core Dialects\n\n- [MySQL](/docs/adapters/mysql)\n- [SQLite](/docs/adapters/sqlite)\n- [PostgreSQL](/docs/adapters/postgresql)\n- [MS SQL](/docs/adapters/mssql)\n\n## Kysely Organization Dialects\n\n- [Postgres.js](https://github.com/kysely-org/kysely-postgres-js)\n- [SingleStore Data API](https://github.com/kysely-org/kysely-singlestore)\n\n\n\n---\n\nchunk 7 | chars: 4121-6017 | source: installation.mdx\n### Create Database Tables\n    Better Auth includes a CLI tool to help manage the schema required by the library.\n\n    - **Generate**: This command generates an ORM schema or SQL migration file.\n\n    <Callout>\n    If you're using Kysely, you can apply the migration directly with `migrate` command below. Use `generate` only if you plan to apply the migration manually.\n    </Callout>\n\n    ```bash title=\"Terminal\"\n    npx @better-auth/cli generate\n    ```\n\n    - **Migrate**: This command creates the required tables directly in the database. (Available only for the built-in Kysely adapter)\n\n    ```bash title=\"Terminal\"\n    npx @better-auth/cli migrate\n    ```\n\n    see the [CLI documentation](/docs/concepts/cli) for more information.\n\n    <Callout>\n     If you instead want to create the schema manually, you can find the core schema required in the [database section](/docs/concepts/database#core-schema).\n    </Callout>\n\n</Step>\n\n<Step>\n\n### Authentication Methods\n\nConfigure the authentication methods you want to use. Better Auth comes with built-in support for email/password, and social sign-on providers.\n\n```ts title=\"auth.ts\"\nimport { betterAuth } from \"better-auth\";\n\nexport const auth = betterAuth({\n  //...other options\n  emailAndPassword: {\n    // [!code highlight]\n    enabled: true, // [!code highlight]\n  }, // [!code highlight]\n  socialProviders: {\n    // [!code highlight]\n    github: {\n      // [!code highlight]\n      clientId: process.env.GITHUB_CLIENT_ID as string, // [!code highlight]\n      clientSecret: process.env.GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET as string, // [!code highlight]\n    }, // [!code highlight]\n  }, // [!code highlight]\n});\n```\n\n<Callout type=\"info\">\nYou can use even more authentication methods like [passkey](/docs/plugins/passkey), [username](/docs/plugins/username), [magic link](/docs/plugins/magic-link) and more through plugins.\n</Callout>\n</Step>\n\n<Step>\n\n\n---\n\nchunk 8 | chars: 276-2221 | source: chars: 11482-12958 | source: basic-usage.mdx\n## Using Plugins\n\nOne of the unique features of Better Auth is a plugins ecosystem. It allows you to add complex auth related functionality with small lines of code.\n\nBelow is an example of how to add two factor authentication using two factor plugin.\n\n<Steps>\n\n<Step>\n### Server Configuration\n\nTo add a plugin, you need to import the plugin and pass it to the `plugins` option of the auth instance. For example, to add two factor authentication, you can use the following code:\n\n```ts title=\"auth.ts\"\nimport { betterAuth } from \"better-auth\"\nimport { twoFactor } from \"better-auth/plugins\" // [!code highlight]\n\nexport const auth = betterAuth({\n    //...rest of the options\n    plugins: [ // [!code highlight]\n        twoFactor() // [!code highlight]\n    ] // [!code highlight]\n})\n```\nnow two factor related routes and method will be available on the server.\n\n</Step>\n<Step>\n### Migrate Database\n\nAfter adding the plugin, you'll need to add the required tables to your database. You can do this by running the `migrate` command, or by using the `generate` command to create the schema and handle the migration manually.\n\ngenerating the schema:\n\n```bash title=\"terminal\"\nnpx @better-auth/cli generate\n```\n\nusing the `migrate` command:\n\n```bash title=\"terminal\"\nnpx @better-auth/cli migrate\n```\n\n<Callout>\nIf you prefer adding the schema manually, you can check the schema required on the [two factor plugin](/docs/plugins/2fa#schema) documentation.\n</Callout>\n\n</Step>\n<Step>\n\n\n---\n\nchunk 10 | chars: 3829-5170 | source: resources.mdx\n## Blog posts\n\n<Resource resources={\n    [\n        {\n\t\t\ttitle: \"Better Auth with Hono, Bun, TypeScript, React and Vite\",\n\t\t\tdescription:\n\t\t\t\t\"You'll learn how to implement authentication with Better Auth in a client - server architecture, where the frontend is separate from the backend.\",\n\t\t\thref: \"https://catalins.tech/better-auth-with-hono-bun-typescript-react-vite\",\n\t\t\ttags: [\"typescript\", \"react\", \"bun\", \"vite\"],\n\t\t},\n\t\t{\n\t\t\ttitle: \"Polar.sh + BetterAuth for Organizations\",\n\t\t\tdescription:\n\t\t\t\t\"Polar.sh is a platform for building payment integrations. ---

You can keep everything in the same Turso/Drizzle database—Better Auth doesn’t require a dedicated instance. Its docs explain that you just pass your existing ORM connection via the Drizzle adapter (`drizzleAdapter(db, { provider: "pg" | "mysql" | "sqlite" })`) so Better Auth tables live alongside your own (`installation.mdx`, `database.mdx`, `drizzle.mdx`).  

When you add Better Auth, run `npx @better-auth/cli generate` to produce the Drizzle schema for the required tables, then run your usual Drizzle migrations (`drizzle-kit generate` + `drizzle-kit migrate`) so those tables join your existing schema (`drizzle.mdx`, `cli.mdx`). If you prefer, you can even map pluralized table names or custom schemas via the adapter options (`drizzle.mdx`).

_**User (2025-11-25 09:36Z)**_

So the generated schema won't replace the actual schema, it will only add the better auth tables that it needs to work no?

_**Agent (model default, mode Agent)**_

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
**Preparing response with documentation references**</details></think>

---

Correct. Running `npx @better-auth/cli generate` just outputs the table definitions Better Auth needs (users, sessions, plugin tables) so you can merge them into your existing Drizzle schema; it does not overwrite your current schema files or database contents. You then apply those additions using your usual Drizzle migration workflow (`drizzle-kit generate` / `drizzle-kit migrate`), which only creates the missing Better Auth tables/columns (`drizzle.mdx`, `cli.mdx`).

create-a-db-adapter.mdx\n---\ntitle: Create a Database Adapter\ndescription: Learn how to create a custom database adapter for Better-Auth\n---\n\nLearn how to create a custom database adapter for Better-Auth using `createAdapter`.\n\nOur `createAdapter` function is designed to be very flexible, and we've done our best to make it easy to understand and use.\nOur hope is to allow you to focus on writing database logic, and not have to worry about how the adapter is working with Better-Auth.\n\nAnything from custom schema configurations, custom ID generation, safe JSON parsing, and more is handled by the `createAdapter` function.\nAll you need to do is provide the database logic, and the `createAdapter` function will handle the rest.\n\n## Quick Start\n\n<Steps>\n<Step>\n### Get things ready\n\n1. Import `createAdapter`.\n2. Create `CustomAdapterConfig` interface that represents your adapter config options.\n3. Create the adapter!\n\n```ts\nimport { createAdapter, type AdapterDebugLogs } from \"better-auth/adapters\";\n\n// Your custom adapter config options\ninterface CustomAdapterConfig {\n  /**\n   * Helps you debug issues with the adapter.\n   */\n  debugLogs?: AdapterDebugLogs;\n  /**\n   * If the table names in the schema are plural.\n   */\n  usePlural?: boolean;\n}\n\nexport const myAdapter = (config: CustomAdapterConfig = {}) =>\n  createAdapter({\n    // ...\n  });\n```\n\n</Step>\n\n<Step>\n\n\n---\n\nchunk 5 | chars: 0-1848 | source: faq.mdx\n---\ntitle: FAQ\ndescription: Frequently asked questions about Better Auth.\n---\n\nThis page contains frequently asked questions, common issues, and other helpful information about Better Auth.\n\n<Accordions>\n  <Accordion title=\"Auth client not working\">\n  When encountering `createAuthClient` related errors, make sure to have the correct import path as it varies based on environment.\n\nIf you're using the auth client on react front-end, you'll need to import it from `/react`:\n\n```ts title=\"component.ts\"\nimport { createAuthClient } from \"better-auth/react\";\n```\n\nWhere as if you're using the auth client in Next.js middleware, server-actions, server-components or anything server-related, you'll likely need to import it from `/client`:\n\n```ts title=\"server.ts\"\nimport { createAuthClient } from \"better-auth/client\";\n```\n\n</Accordion>\n\n<Accordion title=\"getSession not working\">\nIf you try to call `authClient.getSession` on a server environment (e.g, a Next.js server component), it doesn't work since it can't access the cookies. You can use the `auth.api.getSession` instead and pass the request headers to it. \n\n```tsx title=\"server.tsx\"\nimport { auth } from \"./auth\";\nimport { headers } from \"next/headers\";\n\nconst session = await auth.api.getSession({\n    headers: await headers()\n})\n```\n\nif you need to use the auth client on the server for different purposes, you still can pass the request headers to it:\n\n```tsx title=\"server.tsx\"\nimport { authClient } from \"./auth-client\";\nimport { headers } from \"next/headers\";\n\nconst session = await authClient.getSession({\n    fetchOptions:{\n      headers: await headers()\n    }\n})\n```\n</Accordion>\n\n<Accordion title=\"Adding custom fields to the users table\">\n\nBetter Auth provides a type-safe way to extend the user and session schemas, take a look at our docs on <Link href=\"/docs/concepts/database\n\n---\n\nchunk 6 | chars: 328-2300 | source: resources.mdx\n## Video tutorials \n\n<Resource resources={\n    [\n\t\t{\n\t\t\ttitle: This article will show you how to use Better Auth to authenticate your users.\",\n\t\t\thref: \"https://dev.to/phumudzosly/polarsh-betterauth-for-organizations-1j1b\",\n\t\t\ttags: [\"organizations\", \"integration\", \"payments\"],\n\t\t},\n\t\t{\n\t\t\ttitle: \"Authenticating users in Astro with Better Auth\",\n\t\t\tdescription:\n\t\t\t\t\"Step by step guide on how to authenticate users in Astro with Better Auth.\",\n\t\t\thref: \"https://www.launchfa.st/blog/astro-better-auth\",\n\t\t\ttags: [\"astro\", \"integration\", \"tutorial\"],\n\t\t},\n\t\t{\n\t\t\ttitle: \"Building Multi-Tenant Apps With Better-Auth and ZenStack\",\n\t\t\tdescription:\n\t\t\t\t\"Learn how to build multi-tenant apps with Better-Auth and ZenStack.\",\n\t\t\thref: \"https://zenstack.dev/blog/better-auth\",\n\t\t\ttags: [\"multi-tenant\", \"zenstack\", \"architecture\"],\n\t\t},\n    ]\n} />\n\n---\n\nchunk 10 | chars: 0-2116 | source: nitro.mdx\n---\ntitle: Nitro Integration\ndescription: Integrate Better Auth with Nitro.\n---\n\nBetter Auth can be integrated with your [Nitro Application](https://nitro.build/) (an open source framework to build web servers).\n\nThis guide aims to help you integrate Better Auth with your Nitro application in a few simple steps.\n\n## Create a new Nitro Application\n\nStart by scaffolding a new Nitro application using the following command:\n\n```bash title=\"Terminal\"\nnpx giget@latest nitro nitro-app --install\n```\n\nThis will create the `nitro-app` directory and install all the dependencies. You can now open the `nitro-app` directory in your code editor.\n\n### Prisma Adapter Setup\n\n<Callout>\n  This guide assumes that you have a basic understanding of Prisma. If you are new to Prisma, you can check out the [Prisma documentation](https://www.prisma.io/docs/getting-started).\n\n  The `sqlite` database used in this guide will not work in a production environment. You should replace it with a production-ready database like `PostgreSQL`.\n</Callout>\n\nFor this guide, we will be using the Prisma adapter. You can install prisma client by running the following command:\n\n```package-install\n@prisma/client\n```\n\n`prisma` can be installed as a dev dependency using the following command:\n\n```package-install\n-D prisma\n```\n\nGenerate a `schema.prisma` file in the `prisma` directory by running the following command:\n\n```bash title=\"Terminal\"\nnpx prisma init\n```\n\nYou can now replace the contents of the `schema.prisma` file with the following:\n\n```prisma title=\"prisma/schema.prisma\"\ngenerator client {\n  provider = \"prisma-client-js\"\n}\n\ndatasource db {\n  provider = \"sqlite\"\n  url      = env(\"DATABASE_URL\")\n}\n\n// Will be deleted. Just need it to generate the prisma client\nmodel Test {\n  id   Int    @id @default(autoincrement())\n  name String\n}\n```\n\nEnsure that you update the `DATABASE_URL` in your `.env` file to point to the location of your database.\n\n```txt title=\".env\"\nDATABASE_URL=\"file:./dev.db\"\n```\n\nRun the following command to generate the Prisma client & sync the database:\n\n```bash title=\"Terminal\"\nnpx prisma db push\n```\n\n"

"chunk 1 | chars: 0-2039 | source: next.mdx\n---\ntitle: Next.js integration\ndescription: Integrate Better Auth with Next.js.\n---\n\nBetter Auth can be easily integrated with Next.js. Before you start, make sure you have a Better Auth instance configured. If you haven't done that yet, check out the [installation](/docs/installation).\n\n### Create API Route\n\nWe need to mount the handler to an API route. Create a route file inside `/api/auth/[...all]` directory. And add the following code:\n\n```ts title=\"api/auth/[...all]/route.ts\"\nimport { auth } from \"@/lib/auth\";\nimport { toNextJsHandler } from \"better-auth/next-js\";\n\nexport const { GET, POST } = toNextJsHandler(auth.handler);\n```\n\n<Callout type=\"info\">\n You can change the path on your better-auth configuration but it's recommended to keep it as `/api/auth/[...all]`\n</Callout>\n\n\nFor `pages` route, you need to use `toNodeHandler` instead of `toNextJsHandler` and set `bodyParser` to `false` in the `config` object. Here is an example:\n\n```ts title=\"pages/api/auth/[...all].ts\"\nimport { toNodeHandler } from \"better-auth/node\"\nimport { auth } from \"@/lib/auth\"\n\n// Disallow body parsing, we will parse it manually\nexport const config = { api: { bodyParser: false } }\n\nexport default toNodeHandler(auth.handler)\n```\n\n## Create a client\n\nCreate a client instance. You can name the file anything you want. Here we are creating `client.ts` file inside the `lib/` directory.\n\n```ts title=\"auth-client.ts\"\nimport { createAuthClient } from \"better-auth/react\" // make sure to import from better-auth/react\n\nexport const authClient =  createAuthClient({\n    //you can pass client configuration here\n})\n```\n\nOnce you have created the client, you can use it to sign up, sign in, and perform other actions.\nSome of the actions are reactive. The client uses [nano-store](https://github.com/nanostores/nanostores) to store the state and re-render the components when the state changes.\n\nThe client also uses [better-fetch](https://github.com/bekacru/better-fetch) to make the requests. You can pass the fetch configuration to the client.\n\n\n\n\n---\n\nchunk 2 | chars: 3523-5543 | source: next-auth-migration-guide.mdx\n### Update the Client\n\nCreate a file named `auth-client.ts` in the `lib` folder. Add the following code:\n\n```typescript title=\"auth-client.ts\"\nimport { createAuthClient } from \"better-auth/react\";\n\nexport const authClient = createAuthClient({\n    baseURL: process.env.BASE_URL! // Optional if the API base URL matches the frontend\n});\n\nexport const { signIn, signOut, useSession } = authClient;\n```\n\n#### Social Login Functions\n\nUpdate your social login functions to use Better Auth. For example, for Discord:\n\n```typescript\nimport { signIn } from \"~/lib/auth-client\";\n\nexport const signInDiscord = async () => {\n    const data = await signIn.social({\n        provider: \"discord\"\n    });\n    return data;\n};\n```\n\n#### Update `useSession` Calls\n\nReplace `useSession` calls with Better Auth’s version. Example:\n\n```typescript title=\"Profile.tsx\"\nimport { useSession } from \"~/lib/auth-client\";\n\nexport const Profile = () => {\n    const { data } = useSession();\n    return (\n        <div>\n            <pre>\n                {JSON.stringify(data, null, 2)}\n            </pre>\n        </div>\n    );\n};\n```\n</Step>\n\n<Step>\n\n### Server-Side Session Handling\n\nUse the `auth` instance to get session data on the server:\n\n```typescript title=\"actions.ts\"\n\"use server\";\n\nimport { auth } from \"~/server/auth\";\nimport { headers } from \"next/headers\";\n\nexport const protectedAction = async () => {\n    const session = await auth.api.getSession({\n        headers: await headers(),\n    });\n};\n```\n</Step>\n\n<Step>\n### Middleware\n\nTo protect routes with middleware, refer to the [Next.js middleware guide](/docs/integrations/next#middleware).\n</Step>\n</Steps>\n\n\n## Wrapping Up\n\nCongratulations! You’ve successfully migrated from NextAuth.js to Better Auth. For a complete implementation with multiple authentication methods, check out the [demo repository](https://github.com/Bekacru/t3-app-better-auth).\n\nBetter Auth offers greater flexibility and more features—be sure to explore the [documentation](/docs) to unlock its full potential.\n\n\n---\n\nchunk 3 | chars: 6017-7933 | source: installation.mdx\n### Mount Handler\nTo handle API requests, you need to set up a route handler on your server.\n\nCreate a new file or route in your framework's designated catch-all route handler. This route should handle requests for the path `/api/auth/*` (unless you've configured a different base path).\n\n<Callout>\n  Better Auth supports any backend framework with standard Request and Response\n  objects and offers helper functions for popular frameworks.\n</Callout>\n\n<Tabs items={[\"next-js\", \"nuxt\", \"svelte-kit\", \"remix\", \"solid-start\", \"hono\", \"cloudflare-workers\", \"express\", \"elysia\", \"tanstack-start\", \"expo\"]} defaultValue=\"next-js\">\n    <Tab value=\"next-js\">\n        ```ts title=\"/app/api/auth/[...all]/route.ts\"\n        import { auth } from \"@/lib/auth\"; // path to your auth file\n        import { toNextJsHandler } from \"better-auth/next-js\";\n\n        export const { POST, GET } = toNextJsHandler(auth);\n        ```\n    </Tab>\n    <Tab value=\"nuxt\">\n    ```ts title=\"/server/api/auth/[...all].ts\"\n    import { auth } from \"~/utils/auth\"; // path to your auth file\n\n    export default defineEventHandler((event) => {\n        return auth.handler(toWebRequest(event));\n    });\n    ```\n    </Tab>\n    <Tab value=\"svelte-kit\">\n    ```ts title=\"hooks.server.ts\"\n    import { auth } from \"$lib/auth\"; // path to your auth file\n    import { svelteKitHandler } from \"better-auth/svelte-kit\";\n    import { building } from '$app/environment'\n\n    export async function handle({ event, resolve }) {\n        return svelteKitHandler({ event, resolve, auth, building });\n    }\n    ```\n    </Tab>\n    <Tab value=\"remix\">\n    ```ts title=\"/app/routes/api.auth.$.ts\"\n    import { auth } from '~/lib/auth.server' // Adjust the path as necessary\n    import type { LoaderFunctionArgs, ActionFunctionArgs } from \"@remix-run/node\"\n\n    export async function loader({ request }: LoaderFunctionArgs) {\n        return auth.handler(request)\n    }\n\n\n\n---\n\nchunk 4 | chars: 0-1356 | source: next-js.mdx\n---\ntitle: Next.js Example\ndescription: Better Auth Next.js example.\n---\n\nThis is an example of how to use Better Auth with Next.\n\n**Implements the following features:**\nEmail & Password . Social Sign-in . Passkeys . Email Verification . Password Reset . Two Factor Authentication . Profile Update . Session Management . Organization, Members and Roles\n\nSee [Demo](https://demo.better-auth.com)\n\n<ForkButton url=\"better-auth/better-auth/tree/main/demo/nextjs\"  />\n\n<iframe src=\"https://stackblitz.com/github/better-auth/better-auth/tree/main/demo/nextjs?codemirror=1&fontsize=14&hidenavigation=1&runonclick=1&hidedevtools=1\"\n   style={{\n      width: \"100%\",\n      height: \"500px\",\n      border: 0,\n      borderRadius: \"4px\",\n      overflow: \"hidden\"\n   }}\n   title=\"Better Auth Next.js Example\"\n   allow=\"accelerometer; ambient-light-sensor; camera; encrypted-media; geolocation; gyroscope; hid; microphone; midi; payment; usb; vr; xr-spatial-tracking\"\n   sandbox=\"allow-forms allow-modals allow-popups allow-presentation allow-same-origin allow-scripts\"\n   >\n</iframe>\n\n\n## How to run\n\n1. Clone the code sandbox (or the repo) and open it in your code editor\n2. Move .env.example to .env and provide necessary variables\n3. Run the following commands\n   ```bash\n   pnpm install\n   pnpm dev\n   ```\n4. Open the browser and navigate to `http://localhost:3000`\n\n\n---\n\nchunk 5 | chars: 0-1760 | source: express.mdx\n---\ntitle: Express Integration\ndescription: Integrate Better Auth with Express.\n---\n\nThis guide will show you how to integrate Better Auth with [express.js](https://expressjs.com/).\n\nBefore you start, make sure you have a Better Auth instance configured. If you haven't done that yet, check out the [installation](/docs/installation).\n\n<Callout>\nNote that CommonJS (cjs) isn't supported. Use ECMAScript Modules (ESM) by setting `\"type\": \"module\"` in your `package.json` or configuring your `tsconfig.json` to use ES modules.\n</Callout>\n\n### Mount the handler\n\nTo enable Better Auth to handle requests, we need to mount the handler to an API route. Create a catch-all route to manage all requests to `/api/auth/*` in case of ExpressJS v4 or `/api/auth/*splat` in case of ExpressJS v5 (or any other path specified in your Better Auth options).\n\n<Callout type=\"warn\">\nDon’t use `express.json()` before the Better Auth handler. Use it only for other routes, or the client API will get stuck on \"pending\".\n</Callout>\n\n```ts title=\"server.ts\"\nimport express from \"express\";\nimport { toNodeHandler } from \"better-auth/node\";\nimport { auth } from \"./auth\";\n\nconst app = express();\nconst port = 3005;\n\napp.all(\"/api/auth/*\", toNodeHandler(auth)); // For ExpressJS v4\n// app.all(\"/api/auth/*splat\", toNodeHandler(auth)); For ExpressJS v5 \n\n// Mount express json middleware after Better Auth handler\n// or only apply it to routes that don't interact with Better Auth\napp.use(express.json());\n\napp.listen(port, () => {\n\tconsole.log(`Example app listening on port ${port}`);\n});\n```\n\nAfter completing the setup, start your server. Better Auth will be ready to use. You can send a `GET` request to the `/ok` endpoint (`/api/auth/ok`) to verify that the server is running.\n\n\n\n\n---\n\nchunk 6 | chars: 0-1848 | source: faq.mdx\n---\ntitle: FAQ\ndescription: Frequently asked questions about Better Auth.\n---\n\nThis page contains frequently asked questions, common issues, and other helpful information about Better Auth.\n\n<Accordions>\n  <Accordion title=\"Auth client not working\">\n  When encountering `createAuthClient` related errors, make sure to have the correct import path as it varies based on environment.\n\nIf you're using the auth client on react front-end, you'll need to import it from `/react`:\n\n```ts title=\"component.ts\"\nimport { createAuthClient } from \"better-auth/react\";\n```\n\nWhere as if you're using the auth client in Next.js middleware, server-actions, server-components or anything server-related, you'll likely need to import it from `/client`:\n\n```ts title=\"server.ts\"\nimport { createAuthClient } from \"better-auth/client\";\n```\n\n</Accordion>\n\n<Accordion title=\"getSession not working\">\nIf you try to call `authClient.getSession` on a server environment (e.g, a Next.js server component), it doesn't work since it can't access the cookies. You can use the `auth.api.getSession` instead and pass the request headers to it. \n\n```tsx title=\"server.tsx\"\nimport { auth } from \"./auth\";\nimport { headers } from \"next/headers\";\n\nconst session = await auth.api.getSession({\n    headers: await headers()\n})\n```\n\nif you need to use the auth client on the server for different purposes, you still can pass the request headers to it:\n\n```tsx title=\"server.tsx\"\nimport { authClient } from \"./auth-client\";\nimport { headers } from \"next/headers\";\n\nconst session = await authClient.getSession({\n    fetchOptions:{\n      headers: await headers()\n    }\n})\n```\n</Accordion>\n\n<Accordion title=\"Adding custom fields to the users table\">\n\nBetter Auth provides a type-safe way to extend the user and session schemas, take a look at our docs on <Link href=\"/docs/concepts/database\n\n---\n\nchunk 7 | chars: 0-1096 | source: astro.mdx\n---\ntitle: Astro Integration\ndescription: Integrate Better Auth with Astro.\n---\n\nBetter Auth comes with first class support for Astro. Create a file inside `/pages/api/auth` called `[...all].ts` and add the following code:\n\n```ts title=\"pages/api/auth/[...all].ts\"\nimport { auth } from \"~/auth\";\nimport type { APIRoute } from ctx.request.headers.set(\"x-forwarded-for\", ctx.clientAddress);\n\treturn auth.handler(ctx.request);\n};\n```\n\n<Callout>\n    You can change the path on your better-auth configuration but it's recommended to keep it as `/api/auth/[...all]`\n</Callout>\n\n\n\n---\n\nchunk 8 | chars: 328-2300 | source: resources.mdx\n## Video tutorials \n\n<Resource resources={\n    [\n\t\t{\n\t\t\ttitle: recommended to only check for the existence of a session cookie to handle redirection. To avoid blocking requests by making API or database calls.\n\nYou can use the `getSessionCookie` helper from Better Auth for this purpose:\n\n<Callout type=\"warn\">\nThe <code>getSessionCookie()</code> function does not automatically reference the auth config specified in <code>auth.ts</code>. Therefore, if you customized the cookie name or prefix, you need to ensure that the configuration in <code>getSessionCookie()</code> matches the config defined in your <code>auth.ts</code>.\n</Callout>\n\n```ts\nimport { NextRequest, NextResponse } from \"next/server\";\nimport { getSessionCookie } from \"better-auth/cookies\";\n\nexport async function middleware(request: NextRequest) {\n\tconst sessionCookie = getSessionCookie(request);\n\n    // THIS IS NOT SECURE!\n    // This is the recommended approach to optimistically redirect users\n    // We recommend handling auth checks in each page/route\n\tif (!sessionCookie) {\n\t\treturn NextResponse.redirect(new URL(\"/\", request.url));\n\t}\n\n\treturn NextResponse.next();\n}\n\nexport const config = {\n\tmatcher: [\"/dashboard\"], // Specify the routes the middleware applies to\n};\n```\n\n<Callout type=\"warn\">\n\t**Security Warning:** The `getSessionCookie` function only checks for the\n\texistence of a session cookie; it does **not** validate it. Relying solely\n\ton this check for security is dangerous, as anyone can manually create a\n\tcookie to bypass it. You must always validate the session on your server for\n\tany protected actions or pages.\n</Callout>\n\n<Callout type=\"info\">\nIf you have a custom cookie name or prefix, you can pass it to the `getSessionCookie` function.\n```ts\nconst sessionCookie = getSessionCookie(request, {\n    cookieName: \"my_session_cookie\",\n    cookiePrefix: \"my_prefix\"\n});\n```\n</Callout>\n\nAlternatively, you can use the `getCookieCache` helper to get the session object from the cookie cache.\n\n```ts\nimport { getCookieCache } from \"better-auth/cookies\";\n\nexport async function middleware(request: NextRequest) {\n\tconst session = await getCookieCache(request);\n\tif (!session) {\n\t\treturn NextResponse.redirect(new URL(\"/sign-in\", request.url));\n\t}\n\treturn NextResponse.next();\n}\n```\n\n\n\n---\n\nchunk 10 | chars: 3829-5170 | source: resources.mdx\n## Blog posts\n\n<Resource resources={\n    [\n        {\n\t\t\ttitle: \"Better Auth with Hono, Bun, TypeScript, React and Vite\",\n\t\t\tdescription:\n\t\t\t\t\"You'll learn how to implement authentication with Better Auth in a client - server architecture, where the frontend is separate from the backend.\",\n\t\t\thref: \"https://catalins.tech/better-auth-with-hono-bun-typescript-react-vite\",\n\t\t\ttags: [\"typescript\", \"react\", \"bun\", \"vite\"],\n\t\t},\n\t\t{\n\t\t\ttitle: \"Polar.sh + BetterAuth for Organizations\",\n\t\t\tdescription:\n\t\t\t\t\"Polar.sh is a platform for building payment integrations. ## Better Auth + Turso/Drizzle Setup (Next.js 16 App Router)

- **Prereqs**  
  - Turso connection already configured in `db/index.ts`. Keep using it and let Better Auth share the same DB; its CLI only generates the extra tables your auth config needs (`installation.mdx`, `drizzle.mdx`).  
  - Ensure you’re on Node 18+, pnpm installed, and Drizzle CLI already working against Turso.

### 1. Install dependencies
- `pnpm add better-auth better-auth/react better-auth/next-js better-auth/adapters` (the core package also exposes adapters and helpers; install once so you can import `better-auth`, `better-auth/react`, `better-auth/next-js`, `better-auth/adapters/drizzle`).  
- Optional dev tool: `pnpm dlx @better-auth/cli@latest --help` to confirm CLI availability (`cli.mdx`).

### 2. Environment variables
Add to `.env.local` (already gitignored):
```
TURSO_DATABASE_URL="libsql://<db>.turso.io"
TURSO_AUTH_TOKEN="..."
BETTER_AUTH_SECRET="<32+ char random>"
NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL="https://your-domain.com" # keep http://localhost:3000 for dev
```
`BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` is required by Better Auth to sign tokens/sessions.

### 3. Generate schema files
1. Run the Better Auth CLI to scaffold the Drizzle schema for its tables:
   ```
   npx @better-auth/cli@latest generate --output ./db/schema/better-auth.ts
   ```
   - The CLI inspects your `auth.ts` (next step) to know which tables/plugins to emit (`database.mdx`, `cli.mdx`).
   - Result: `db/schema/better-auth.ts` containing `users`, `sessions`, `accounts`, etc.
2. Expose those tables through your Drizzle schema barrel (`db/schema/index.ts` if you have one) so migrations pick them up.

### 4. Wire Better Auth to Drizzle/Turso
Create `lib/auth.ts`:

```
import { betterAuth } from "better-auth";
import { drizzleAdapter } from "better-auth/adapters/drizzle";
import { db } from "@/db";                    // existing Turso Drizzle instance
import * as authSchema from "@/db/schema/better-auth";

export const auth = betterAuth({
  secret: process.env.BETTER_AUTH_SECRET!,
  database: drizzleAdapter(db, {
    provider: "sqlite",                      // Turso/libSQL uses sqlite dialect
    schema: {
      ...authSchema,
      user: authSchema.users,                // map singular if needed (drizzle.mdx)
    },
  }),
  emailAndPassword: { enabled: true },       // enable desired methods
  socialProviders: {
    github: {
      clientId: process.env.GITHUB_CLIENT_ID!,
      clientSecret: process.env.GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET!,
    },
  },
});
```
- Add/adjust plugins (passkeys, 2FA, etc.) here; CLI regenerates schema when config changes (`installation.mdx`, `drizzle.mdx`, `basic-usage.mdx`).

### 5. Mount the handler (App Router)
Create `app/api/auth/[...all]/route.ts`:

```
import { auth } from "@/lib/auth";
import { toNextJsHandler } from "better-auth/next-js";

export const { GET, POST } = toNextJsHandler(auth.handler);
```
Docs recommend the `/api/auth/[...all]` catch-all for Next.js 16 (`next.mdx`, `installation.mdx`).

### 6. Client-side helper
Create `lib/auth-client.ts`:

```
import { createAuthClient } from "better-auth/react";

export const authClient = createAuthClient({
  baseURL: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL, // optional if same origin
});

export const { signIn, signOut, useSession } = authClient;
```
Use `authClient` inside React components; it keeps session state via nanostores (`next.mdx`, `next-auth-migration-guide.mdx`, `faq.mdx`).

### 7. Server utilities
- In server components/actions, call `auth.api.getSession({ headers: await headers() })` to validate the user.  
- Optional middleware: use `getSessionCookie` or `getCookieCache` from `better-auth/cookies` for cheap redirects, but still guard sensitive routes on the server (`next.mdx`).

### 8. Run migrations against Turso
1. Ensure `db/drizzle.config.ts` points to Turso URL/auth token.  
2. Generate migrations with both your CMS tables and Better Auth tables now in the schema:
   ```
   pnpm drizzle-kit generate
   ```
3. Apply to Turso:
   ```
   pnpm drizzle-kit push   # or pnpm drizzle-kit migrate
   ```
   Better Auth tables live in the same DB; nothing gets overwritten—only missing tables/columns are created (`drizzle.mdx`).

### 9. Folder layout snapshot
```
/lib
  auth.ts
  auth-client.ts
/app
  /api/auth/[...all]/route.ts
/db
  drizzle.config.ts
  index.ts
  /schema
    cms-tables.ts
    better-auth.ts        # generated
    index.ts
/env files (.env.local)   # contains Turso + Better Auth secrets
```

### 10. Validation checklist
- `pnpm dev` → hit `GET /api/auth/ok` to confirm handler responds 200 (`installation.mdx`).  
- Create a test user via `authClient.signUp.email()` or `curl` to ensure Turso tables populate.  
- Add UI screens (sign in/up, profile) using `authClient` hooks; protect server routes with `auth.api.*`.

This flow keeps Better Auth tables inside the same Turso/Drizzle database, leverages the CLI for schema generation, and plugs straight into your Next.js 16 app router.

## Better Auth Setup (pnpm, Next.js 16 App Router, Drizzle + Turso)

**1. Install the package**  
- `pnpm add better-auth` is enough; the package exposes server, adapter, Next.js, and React helpers from one install (`installation.mdx`).

**2. Set environment variables** (`.env.local`)  
- `TURSO_DATABASE_URL`, `TURSO_AUTH_TOKEN` for your existing Turso connection.  
- `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` (32+ random characters) required for session signing.  
- Any provider creds you plan to enable (e.g., `GITHUB_CLIENT_ID`). (`installation.mdx`, `database.mdx`)

**3. Create a Better Auth instance** → `lib/auth.ts`  
```ts
import { betterAuth } from "better-auth";
import { drizzleAdapter } from "better-auth/adapters/drizzle";
import { db } from "@/db";                 // your Drizzle Turso client
import * as authSchema from "@/db/schema/better-auth";

export const auth = betterAuth({
  secret: process.env.BETTER_AUTH_SECRET!,
  database: drizzleAdapter(db, {
    provider: "sqlite",                   // Turso/libSQL uses sqlite dialect
    schema: { ...authSchema, user: authSchema.users },
  }),
  emailAndPassword: { enabled: true },    // configure in step 6
});
```
(`installation.mdx`, `drizzle.mdx`)

**4. Configure database (Drizzle + Turso)**  
- Keep using `db/index.ts` to instantiate Drizzle with Turso’s URL/token.  
- The Drizzle adapter just wraps that `db` instance; `provider: "sqlite"` is the correct value for Turso.  
- If your Drizzle tables are plural, either map manually (as above) or pass `usePlural: true`. (`drizzle.mdx`)

**5. Create database tables**  
1. Generate schema files from your Better Auth config:  
   `npx @better-auth/cli@latest generate --output ./db/schema/better-auth.ts`  
   (CLI just adds definitions for Better Auth tables; it doesn’t overwrite your own schema.)  
2. Run Drizzle migrations so those tables are created in Turso:  
   `pnpm drizzle-kit generate` → `pnpm drizzle-kit push` (or `migrate`). (`cli.mdx`, `drizzle.mdx`)

**6. Authentication methods** (still `lib/auth.ts`)  
- Enable built-ins by toggling options inside the `betterAuth` call.  
```ts
emailAndPassword: { enabled: true },
socialProviders: {
  github: {
    clientId: process.env.GITHUB_CLIENT_ID!,
    clientSecret: process.env.GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET!,
  },
},
```
- Add plugins (passkey, username, etc.) via the `plugins` array; rerun `generate` if schema changes. (`installation.mdx`, `basic-usage.mdx`)

**7. Mount handler (Next.js App Router)** → `app/api/auth/[...all]/route.ts`  
```ts
import { auth } from "@/lib/auth";
import { toNextJsHandler } from "better-auth/next-js";

export const { GET, POST } = toNextJsHandler(auth.handler);
```
- Keep the route at `/api/auth/[...all]` unless you configure a different base path. (`next.mdx`, `installation.mdx`)

**8. Create client instance** → `lib/auth-client.ts`  
```ts
import { createAuthClient } from "better-auth/react";

export const authClient = createAuthClient({
  baseURL: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL, // optional if same origin
});

export const { signIn, signOut, useSession } = authClient;
```
- Use `authClient` in React components; for server components/actions call `auth.api.getSession({ headers: await headers() })`. (`next.mdx`, `next-auth-migration-guide.mdx`, `faq.mdx`)

With these eight steps, Better Auth shares your Turso/Drizzle database, exposes the Next.js handler, and provides both server and client utilities per the MCP docs.

   ```

   ```
   pnpx @better-auth/cli@latest generate --output ./db/schema/better-auth.ts
   ```

Once the CLI writes the schema, TypeScript will resolve the import and you can proceed with migrations.

Yep—you can drop `baseURL` entirely. Better Auth’s React client defaults to the current origin, so if your Next.js frontend and API share the same domain (which they do in this full-stack setup), there’s no need to pass it. Only set `baseURL` when the UI talks to a different host (e.g., separate frontend domain or mobile app).

**Not redundant, just two equivalent ways to configure it.**

- If you **omit** `secret` in `betterAuth({ ... })`, Better Auth will automatically read it from env: **`BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` or `AUTH_SECRET`** (`options.mdx`). That’s usually what you want in a Next.js app.
- If you **pass `secret: process.env.BETTER_AUTH_SECRET!` explicitly**, you’re just wiring the same value manually; behavior is the same as long as the env var is set.

So in your `auth.ts` you can safely remove `secret: process.env.BETTER_AUTH_SECRET!` and rely on the env variable alone, unless you specifically want to override the env or make the source more explicit.

Create a route file inside `/api/auth/[...all]` directory. And add the following code:\n\n```ts title=\"api/auth/[...all]/route.ts\"\nimport { auth } from \"@/lib/auth\";\nimport { toNextJsHandler } from \"better-auth/next-js\";\n\nexport const { GET, POST } = toNextJsHandler(auth.handler);\n```\n\n<Callout type=\"info\">\n You can change the path on your better-auth configuration but it's recommended to keep it as `/api/auth/[...all]`\n</Callout>\n\n\nFor `pages` route, you need to use `toNodeHandler` instead of `toNextJsHandler` and set `bodyParser` to `false` in the `config` object. Here is an example:\n\n```ts title=\"pages/api/auth/[...all].ts\"\nimport { toNodeHandler } from \"better-auth/node\"\nimport { auth } from \"@/lib/auth\"\n\n// Disallow body parsing, we will parse it manually\nexport const config = { api: { bodyParser: false } }\n\nexport default toNodeHandler(auth.handler)\n```\n\n## Create a client\n\nCreate a client instance. You can name the file anything you want. ### Do you need separate login/logout route handlers?

**No.** With Better Auth + Next.js App Router, you **do not** create custom `/login` or `/logout` API route handlers. The single catch‑all handler you already have:

```ts
// app/api/auth/[...all]/route.ts
import { auth } from "@/lib/auth";
import { toNextJsHandler } from "better-auth/next-js";

export const { GET, POST } = toNextJsHandler(auth.handler);
```

is enough to expose **all** Better Auth endpoints (sign in, sign out, sign up, etc.) under `/api/auth/*` (`next.mdx`, `installation.mdx`).

### What you do instead (step by step)

1. **Keep the catch‑all route** above exactly as is – that’s your only server handler for auth.
2. **Use the client in your UI**, e.g. in `lib/auth-client.ts` you already have:

   ```ts
   import { createAuthClient } from "better-auth/react";

   export const authClient = createAuthClient({});
   export const { signIn, signOut, useSession } = authClient;
   ```

3. **Call auth actions from components**:
   - Email/password login: `await signIn.email({ email, password })`
   - Signup: `await authClient.signUp.email({ email, password })` (or `signIn` variants depending on method)
   - Logout: `await signOut()`  

   These functions automatically talk to `/api/auth/[...all]`; you don’t wire any extra routes yourself (`next.mdx`, `next-auth-migration-guide.mdx`).

So: one catch‑all route handler + client methods in your components = full login/logout flow; no additional route handlers required.

### Short answer

**Yes, you should set this up.** With Better Auth, the **correct way to get the current user in Server Actions / Route Handlers** is via `auth.api.getSession({ headers })`. This reads the session cookie from the incoming request headers and returns the validated session. It’s not automatic—you must call it when you need the session.

---

### Why this matters (in simple terms)

- **Server Actions run on the server** and don’t have direct access to `document.cookie` or the Better Auth React client.
- Better Auth stores the session using cookies + your DB; **validation happens on the server**.
- Calling `auth.api.getSession`:
  - Verifies the cookie is real and not tampered with.
  - Loads the corresponding session/user from your Turso DB.
  - Lets you safely gate actions like “create project”, “update profile”, etc.

You *can* build without this at first, but as soon as you have any “only logged‑in users can do X” on the server, you need it.

---

### Step‑by‑step: make session retrievable in Server Actions

#### 1. Ensure `auth` is set up (you already have this)

`lib/auth.ts`:

```ts
import { betterAuth } from "better-auth";
import { drizzleAdapter } from "better-auth/adapters/drizzle";
import { db } from "@/db";
import * as authSchema from "@/db/schema/better-auth";

export const auth = betterAuth({
  database: drizzleAdapter(db, {
    provider: "sqlite",
    schema: { ...authSchema, user: authSchema.users },
    usePlural: true,
  }),
  emailAndPassword: { enabled: true },
});
```

#### 2. Create a small server helper to read the session

Create `lib/server-session.ts`:

```ts
import "server-only";
import { headers } from "next/headers";
import { auth } from "@/lib/auth";

export async function getServerSession() {
  const session = await auth.api.getSession({
    headers: await headers(),
  });

  return session;
}
```

- `headers()` gives you the incoming request headers (including cookies) in App Router.
- Better Auth uses those headers to read & validate the session cookie.

*(Pattern based on Better Auth FAQ’s `auth.api.getSession({ headers: await headers() })` usage.)*

#### 3. Use it inside Server Actions

Example: `app/actions/protected.ts`:

```ts
"use server";

import { getServerSession } from "@/lib/server-session";

export async function createProtectedResource(formData: FormData) {
  const session = await getServerSession();

  if (!session) {
    throw new Error("Not authenticated");
  }

  // session.user.id is now safe to use
  const userId = session.user.id;
  // ... do your DB work with userId (Turso via Drizzle)
}
```

- `session` will be `null`/`undefined` if the user is not logged in.
- You can throw, return an error, or redirect based on your UX needs.

#### 4. Use the same helper in Route Handlers

Example: `app/api/me/route.ts`:

```ts
import { NextResponse } from "next/server";
import { getServerSession } from "@/lib/server-session";

export async function GET() {
  const session = await getServerSession();

  if (!session) {
    return new NextResponse("Unauthorized", { status: 401 });
  }

  return NextResponse.json({ user: session.user });
}
```

---

### When to reach for this

Use `getServerSession()` (i.e. `auth.api.getSession`) whenever:

- A **Server Action** should only run for authenticated users.
- A **Route Handler** should return data based on the current user.
- You need `user.id` or other user fields safely on the server.

On the **client**, keep using your `authClient`:

```ts
const { data: session } = useSession();
await signIn.email({ email, password });
await signOut();
```

On the **server**, always go through `auth.api.getSession` with `headers` as above.

Cookie caching handles this by storing session data in a short-lived, signed cookie similar to how JWT access tokens are used with refresh tokens.\n\nTo turn on cookie caching, just set `session.cookieCache` in your auth config:\n\n```ts title=\"auth.ts\"\nimport { betterAuth } from \"better-auth\";\n\nexport const auth = betterAuth({\n  session: {\n    cookieCache: {\n      enabled: true,\n      maxAge: 5 * 60, // Cache duration in seconds\n    },\n  },\n});\n```\n\nRead more about [cookie caching](/docs/concepts/session-management\n\n---\n\nchunk 3 | chars: 3790-6004 | source: session-management.mdx\n### Revoke Other Sessions\n\nTo revoke all other sessions except the current session, you can use the `revokeOtherSessions` function.\n\n```ts title=\"auth-client.ts\"\nawait authClient.revokeOtherSessions()\n```\n\n### Revoke All Sessions\n\nTo revoke all sessions, you can use the `revokeSessions` function.\n\n```ts title=\"auth-client.ts\"\nawait authClient.revokeSessions()\n```\n\n### Revoking Sessions on Password Change\n\nYou can revoke all sessions when the user changes their password by passing `revokeOtherSessions` as true on `changePassword` function.\n\n```ts title=\"auth.ts\"\nawait authClient.changePassword({\n    newPassword: newPassword,\n    currentPassword: currentPassword,\n    revokeOtherSessions: true,\n})\n```\n\n## Session Caching\n\n### Cookie Cache\n\nCalling your database every time `useSession` or `getSession` invoked isn’t ideal, especially if sessions don’t change frequently. Cookie caching handles this by storing session data in a short-lived, signed cookie—similar to how JWT access tokens are used with refresh tokens.\n\nWhen cookie caching is enabled, the server can check session validity from the cookie itself instead of hitting the database each time.    }\n    }\n});\n```\n\nIf you want to disable returning from the cookie cache when fetching the session, you can pass `disableCookieCache:true` this will force the server to fetch the session from });\n});\n```\n\n\n\n### Context\n\nThe `ctx` object contains another `context` object inside that's meant to hold contexts related to auth. ### Big picture

- **Middleware / proxy layer:** Use **cheap, optimistic, cookie-based checks** only, just to decide simple redirects (e.g. “if user *seems* logged in, send them away from `/login` to `/dashboard`”).
- **Pages / routes / server actions:** Use **`auth.api.getSession()`** (optionally with cookie cache) for **real, secure auth** — this is where you actually decide “is this user allowed to do X”.

This lines up perfectly with the new **proxy-style middleware** in Next.js and with Better Auth’s own middleware docs.

---

### 1. `getSessionCookie` – what it does and when to use it

From the Better Auth docs (`next.mdx`):

- Middleware example:

```ts
import { NextRequest, NextResponse } from "next/server";
import { getSessionCookie } from "better-auth/cookies";

export async function middleware(request: NextRequest) {
  const sessionCookie = getSessionCookie(request);

  // THIS IS NOT SECURE!
  // Recommended for optimistic redirects only.
  if (!sessionCookie) {
    return NextResponse.redirect(new URL("/", request.url));
  }

  return NextResponse.next();
}
```

- Key points:
  - **Only checks if a session cookie exists**.
  - **Does NOT validate** that the cookie is legit, unexpired, or tied to a real DB session.
  - Docs explicitly warn: relying solely on this is **dangerous**, because a user can forge a cookie string; only the server-side validation (via Better Auth) knows if it’s valid.

**Where it fits in your “proxy.ts” idea:**

- In your **proxy/middleware** file, you:
  - Call `getSessionCookie(request)`.
  - If truthy, treat the user as “probably logged in” and do UX redirections:
    - e.g. block `/sign-in` for “logged-in” users.
  - If falsy, redirect them away from `/dashboard` to `/sign-in`.

- You **never** use this to gate DB writes, protected API logic, etc. It’s strictly a **UX optimization**.

---

### 2. `auth.api.getSession` – what it does and when to use it

From the FAQ and session docs:

```ts
import { auth } from "@/lib/auth";
import { headers } from "next/headers";

const session = await auth.api.getSession({
  headers: await headers(),
});
```

- What it does:
  - Reads the **session cookie + related cookies** from the headers.
  - **Validates**:
    - Signature (cookie hasn’t been tampered with).
    - Expiry.
    - That the session still exists in your DB (Turso via Drizzle).
  - Optionally uses **cookieCache** to avoid hitting the DB for every call (see next section).

**Where it fits in your app:**

- **Server Actions** (“use server”):
  - Before doing any privileged operation, call `auth.api.getSession({ headers: await headers() })`.
  - If `!session`, treat as unauthenticated.
- **Route Handlers** (`app/api/...`):
  - Same pattern as above; use the validated `session.user.id` for Turso queries.
- **Server Components**:
  - You can also call `auth.api.getSession` directly to get the user for rendering.

This is your **real security boundary** – this is what prevents forged cookies and handles revoked/expired sessions correctly.

---

### 3. Cookie-based checks, `getCookieCache`, and performance

Better Auth adds a **cookie cache** concept to avoid hammering your DB:

From `optimizing-for-performance.mdx` / `session-management.mdx`:

- Enable cookie cache in `auth` config:

```ts
export const auth = betterAuth({
  session: {
    cookieCache: {
      enabled: true,
      maxAge: 5 * 60, // seconds
    },
  },
});
```

- With this:
  - When a session is fetched and confirmed, Better Auth stores a **short-lived, signed snapshot** of the session in a cookie (like a JWT-style access token + DB refresh token).
  - Future `getSession` calls can often validate from this cookie without a DB query.
- You can **force bypass** it when you need fresh data:

```ts
await auth.api.getSession({
  headers: req.headers,
  query: { disableCookieCache: true },
});
```

In middleware, there’s also:

```ts
import { getCookieCache } from "better-auth/cookies";

export async function middleware(request: NextRequest) {
  const session = await getCookieCache(request);
  if (!session) {
    return NextResponse.redirect(new URL("/sign-in", request.url));
  }
  return NextResponse.next();
}
```

- `getCookieCache`:
  - Reads the **signed, cached session data** from the cookie.
  - Still faster than a DB hit, but **more informative** than just `getSessionCookie` (you get user data).
  - Still **not where you put critical auth logic** – if something really matters, you should still validate via `auth.api.getSession` in the route/action.

---

### 4. How this maps to the new Next.js proxy-style middleware

Given your goal: **“proxy only does redirects; real auth checks live in pages/routes”**, the pattern is:

- **`proxy.ts` / `middleware.ts` (edge / proxy layer)**  
  - Use `getSessionCookie` (or `getCookieCache` if you want more info) **purely for redirect decisions**:
    - If session cookie present → redirect from `/sign-in` to `/dashboard`.
    - If session cookie missing → redirect from `/dashboard` to `/sign-in`.
  - No DB calls, no `auth.api.getSession` here; keeps it fast and avoids old “middleware does heavy auth” pitfalls.

- **Pages / Route Handlers / Server Actions (origin layer)**  
  - Use `auth.api.getSession({ headers })` for **authoritative checks**:
    - Protect mutations (create/update/delete).
    - Protect sensitive data reads.
    - Derive `userId` for Turso queries.
  - This is where you enforce **real security guarantees**.

This design:

- Matches Better Auth’s own recommendation: “use `getSessionCookie` for optimistic redirects; handle auth checks in each page/route.”
- Matches the newer Next.js guidance: use middleware as a **proxy/edge prefilter**, not as your main auth engine.

---

### 5. TL;DR guidelines for you

- **In proxy/middleware:**  
  - Use **`getSessionCookie(request)`** or **`getCookieCache(request)`**.  
  - Only redirect or lightly shape traffic.  
  - Assume cookies can be faked → this layer is for UX, not true security.

- **In pages/routes/server actions:**  
  - Use **`auth.api.getSession({ headers: await headers() })`**.  
  - Make all **“is user allowed to do this?”** decisions here.  
  - Optionally leverage `cookieCache` for performance, but still through `auth.api.getSession`.

If you want, next step we can sketch a concrete `proxy.ts` for your repo that only uses `getSessionCookie` for redirects and leaves everything else to your existing route logic.

---

You can absolutely pair Better Auth with React’s `cache()` helper to make per-request auth checks more efficient. The idea:

- `auth.api.getSession({ headers })` is the secure call you run in pages/routes/server actions.  
- In a single request you might need that session more than once (e.g., layout + page + server action). Without caching, each call repeats the same cookie parsing and DB lookup.

Wrap it in `cache()` so the first call does the work and subsequent calls reuse the result:

```ts
// lib/get-server-session.ts
import "server-only";
import { cache } from "react";
import { headers } from "next/headers";
import { auth } from "@/lib/auth";

export const getServerSession = cache(async () => {
  return auth.api.getSession({
    headers: await headers(),
  });
});
```

Now anywhere on the server (Server Components, Route Handlers, Server Actions) you can:

```ts
const session = await getServerSession();
if (!session) throw new Error("Not authenticated");
```

Why use `cache()`?

- **Per-request memoization:** Next.js resets caches for each request, so you’re safe from cross-user leaks.
- **Performance:** Avoids hitting Turso or revalidating cookies multiple times when your tree renders the same helper repeatedly.
- **Clean ergonomics:** All server code imports the same `getServerSession` helper; you don’t duplicate `headers()`/`auth.api.getSession` everywhere.

Combine this with your middleware proxy strategy:
- Middleware only does cookie existence checks + redirects.
- Pages/routes use `await getServerSession()` (cached) for real authorization.

If you enable Better Auth’s cookie cache in `auth.ts`, `auth.api.getSession` itself can often serve from the signed cache cookie, and the React `cache()` layer just avoids calling that twice in one request—stacking both optimizations.

You’ve got a few good patterns to choose from—use whatever keeps each action easy to find, test, and reuse. Here’s how most teams structure them:

### 1. Dedicated server-action modules (recommended)
- Put each logical domain in its own file, e.g. `app/actions/users.ts`, `app/actions/projects.ts`.
- Export named async functions: `export async function updateProfile(formData: FormData) { … }`.
- Import those actions wherever needed (components, route handlers).  
**Why:** keeps logic centralized, testable, and sharable across multiple components while avoiding giant files.

### 2. Co-locate per route/component when scope is tiny
- For a one-off action tied tightly to a single page, you can define it inline in that component or in the same file.
- Just add `"use server"` atop the function or file.  
**Why:** reduces indirection for truly local actions, but avoid this if multiple components need the same action.

### 3. Action groups per feature
- Some teams create folders like `app/(dashboard)/actions.ts` or `app/(marketing)/actions/`.
- Combine with React’s `cache()` helper + shared auth utility (`getServerSession`) so each action imports consistent helpers.

### 4. Route handlers or RPC-style endpoints
- If you need fine-grained HTTP control (streaming, custom status codes) you can still use `/app/api/...` routes with `auth.api.getSession`.
- Server Actions are faster to wire up, but routes give more HTTP flexibility.

### Tips regardless of layout
- Keep each file focused (3-6 related actions max) so diffs stay readable.
- Reuse shared helpers (`getServerSession`, Drizzle queries) to avoid drifting logic.
- If an action grows complex, split it into private utility functions in the same module or a `lib/` helper.

In short: default to feature-based modules of named server actions; go inline only for one-off UI-specific work; and fall back to Next.js route handlers if you hit Server Action limitations.

import "server-only";

#### 2. Use it in your Server Actions

import { redirect } from "next/navigation";

  const session = await getServerSession();

  if (!session) {
    throw new Error("Not authenticated");
    // or: redirect("/sign-in");
  }

  // session.user is now safe to use

  // ... do your DB work (Turso via Drizzle)
}

---

#### 3. (Optional) Revalidate or redirect after mutations

```ts
"use server";

import { revalidatePath } from "next/cache";
import { redirect } from "next/navigation";
import { getServerSession } from "@/lib/server-session";

export async function createPost(formData: FormData) {
  const session = await getServerSession();
  if (!session) throw new Error("Not authenticated");

  // ... insert into DB using session.user.id

  revalidatePath("/posts");
  redirect("/posts");
}
```

| Client Components | `useSession()` from `lib/auth-client.ts` |

```ts
// middleware.ts (at project root)
import { NextRequest, NextResponse } from "next/server";
import { getSessionCookie } from "better-auth/cookies";

export function middleware(request: NextRequest) {
  const sessionCookie = getSessionCookie(request);
  const { pathname } = request.nextUrl;

  // If user seems logged in, redirect away from auth pages
  if (sessionCookie && pathname.startsWith("/sign-in")) {
    return NextResponse.redirect(new URL("/dashboard", request.url));
  }

  // If user seems logged out, redirect away from protected pages
  if (!sessionCookie && pathname.startsWith("/dashboard")) {
    return NextResponse.redirect(new URL("/sign-in", request.url));
  }

  return NextResponse.next();
}

export const config = {
  matcher: ["/sign-in", "/dashboard/:path*"],
};
```

Good catch! There are **two different approaches** in the Better Auth docs, and they serve different purposes:

---

## Approach 1: `getSessionCookie` (what you have now)

```ts
export function middleware(request: NextRequest) {
  const sessionCookie = getSessionCookie(request);
  // ...
}
```

- **Sync** (no `async`)
- **Runs on Edge runtime** (default for `middleware.ts`)
- **Only checks if cookie EXISTS** — no validation
- **Fast** — no DB call, no API call
- **NOT secure** — anyone can forge a cookie

---

## Approach 2: `auth.api.getSession` (the docs example you found)

```ts
export async function proxy(request: NextRequest) {
  const session = await auth.api.getSession({
    headers: await headers()
  });
  // ...
}

export const config = {
  runtime: "nodejs", // REQUIRED
  matcher: ["/dashboard"],
};
```

- **Async** — because it calls the database
- **Requires `runtime: "nodejs"`** — Edge runtime can't run Drizzle/Turso
- **Actually VALIDATES the session** — checks DB, signature, expiry
- **Slower** — hits your Turso DB on every matched request
- **More secure in middleware** — but still recommends checking in pages/routes

### Why `headers()` instead of `request`?

In Next.js 16, `auth.api.getSession` expects a standard `Headers` object. The `headers()` function from `next/headers` returns exactly that. You *could* also pass `request.headers`, but `headers()` is the canonical App Router way and works consistently across middleware, Server Components, and Route Handlers.

---

## Which should you use?

| Approach | When to use |
|----------|-------------|
| `getSessionCookie` (sync, edge) | **UX-only redirects** — fast, but not secure |
| `auth.api.getSession` (async, nodejs) | **If you want validated session in middleware** — slower but accurate |

**Better Auth's own recommendation:** Use the fast cookie check in middleware for UX, then do **real validation in each page/route** via `getServerSession()`.

---

## For your setup

Since you want the **proxy approach with real validation**, rename and update your file:

```ts
// proxy.ts (at project root)
import { NextRequest, NextResponse } from "next/server";
import { headers } from "next/headers";
import { auth } from "@/lib/auth";

export async function proxy(request: NextRequest) {
  const session = await auth.api.getSession({
    headers: await headers()
  });

  const { pathname } = request.nextUrl;

  // Redirect logged-in users away from auth pages
  if (session && pathname.startsWith("/sign-in")) {
    return NextResponse.redirect(new URL("/dashboard", request.url));
  }

  // Redirect logged-out users away from protected pages
  if (!session && pathname.startsWith("/dashboard")) {
    return NextResponse.redirect(new URL("/sign-in", request.url));
  }

  return NextResponse.next();
}

export const config = {
  runtime: "nodejs", // Required for auth.api calls with Drizzle/Turso
  matcher: ["/sign-in", "/dashboard/:path*"],
};
```

**Note:** Next.js looks for `middleware.ts` by default. If you want to use `proxy.ts` as the filename, you'll need to configure Next.js to recognize it, or just rename it to `middleware.ts`.

---

## TL;DR

| | `getSessionCookie` | `auth.api.getSession` |
|---|---|---|
| Runtime | Edge (default) | Node.js (must set) |
| Async | No | Yes |
| Validates session | ❌ No | ✅ Yes |
| Speed | Fast | Slower (DB call) |
| Security | Not secure | More secure |

Both approaches still recommend doing **final auth checks in pages/routes** — middleware is just for UX convenience.

### 1. `lib/auth.ts` — Cookie cache enabled

```ts
session: {
    cookieCache: {
        enabled: true,
        maxAge: 5 * 60, // 5 minutes
    },
},
```

This stores a signed session snapshot in a cookie so `getSession` doesn't hit Turso on every call.

---

### 2. `lib/actions/auth.ts` — Simple test action

```ts
"use server";

import { getServerSession } from "@/lib/server-session";

export async function testSessionAction() {
    const session = await getServerSession();

    if (!session) {
        return { success: false, error: "Not authenticated" };
    }

    return {
        success: true,
        user: {
            id: session.user.id,
            email: session.user.email,
            name: session.user.name,
        },
    };
}
```

Returns user data if authenticated, error if not. No redirect/revalidate needed for a simple read.
